body:
## Summary

On a dtplyr input, a factor column carrying a declared `NA` level loses it whenever
it crosses the branch union without being a Margin dimension — as a fixed `.by` key,
or as a column the verb passes through. The same call on the same data through the
local `data.frame` backend keeps it, so the result's column domain differs by backend
with no error, warning, or other diagnostic.

This is the residual of #408, which fixed the dimension case only. It was found by
the review of that branch (#413) and left as a ticket rather than widened into it,
because #408's Summary and Implementation site are both about a Margin *dimension*.

## Reproduction

```r
pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

data <- data.frame(
  key = structure(c(1L, 2L), levels = c("p", NA_character_), class = "factor"),
  passthrough = structure(c(1L, 2L), levels = c("a", NA_character_), class = "factor"),
  group = factor(c("g1", "g2")),
  value = 1:2
)

fixed_key <- function(input) {
  summarize_with_margins(
    input, n = dplyr::n(), .by = key, .grouping = rollup(group)
  )
}
cat("fixed .by key -- local:  "); print(levels(fixed_key(data)$key))
cat("fixed .by key -- dtplyr: ")
print(levels(dplyr::collect(fixed_key(dtplyr::lazy_dt(data)))$key))

passthrough <- function(input) {
  expand_with_margins(input, .grouping = rollup(group))
}
cat("passthrough  -- local:  "); print(levels(passthrough(data)$passthrough))
cat("passthrough  -- dtplyr: ")
print(levels(dplyr::collect(passthrough(dtplyr::lazy_dt(data)))$passthrough))
```

## Observed / Expected

Observed, verbatim, at the head of the #408 branch:

```
fixed .by key -- local:  [1] "p" NA 
fixed .by key -- dtplyr: [1] "p"
passthrough  -- local:  [1] "a" NA 
passthrough  -- dtplyr: [1] "a"
```

Expected: each dtplyr line is `[1] "p" NA` and `[1] "a" NA` respectively, as its local
line is. Nothing else in the output changes.

## Contract violated

ADR 0016, *The promise boundary*:

> marginplyr constructs, and therefore promises:
>
> [...]
> - factor and ordered-factor levels, ordering, and Margin-label placement, per
>   ADR 0012.

That clause is not qualified to Margin dimensions, and neither is ADR 0012's sixth row.
Whether it should be is the first question this ticket has to answer — a `.by` key and a
passed-through column are columns marginplyr does not label, and ADR 0016 elsewhere
separates what it constructs from what it passes through. If the boundary places them on
the passed-through side, the answer is an amendment saying so rather than code.

## Root cause

The same one as #408: `data.table`'s rbind drops a declared `NA` level from the result
and turns the values that used it into missing codes, for a list of one table as much as
for a union of branches.

```r
f <- structure(c(1L, 1L), levels = c("x", NA_character_), class = "factor")
a <- data.table::data.table(group = f)
levels(data.table::rbindlist(list(a))$group)
#> [1] "x"
```

#408 answered it by routing a factor *dimension* whose Margin label is missing through
the same encode-and-rebuild path a labelled one already took — the
`drops_na_factor_level_on_union` capability in `backend_capabilities()`, read per column
as `encode_missing_label` in `margin_column_info()`. That route is reached from
`label_margin_branch()` and `restore_margin_factors()`, both of which iterate
`plan$dimensions` only.

## What is unmeasured

- Whether a passed-through column can be routed at all. `margin_column_info()` reads the
  selection proxy for `plan$dimensions`; a passthrough column's levels are not acquired
  today, and ADR 0002 (*acquire typed metadata once*) is where widening that read would
  have to be argued.
- The cost of acquiring and restoring levels for every factor column of a wide input,
  against acquiring them for the dimensions alone.
- Whether the ordered-factor and Margin-label-position rules have anything to say about a
  column that carries no Margin label.

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Route every factor column crossing the dtplyr branch union through the encode-and-rebuild path, not only Margin dimensions

**Current behavior:**

Reproduced verbatim at `842f156`, with the Reproduction section of this issue.
Both dtplyr lines lose the declared `NA` level while their local counterparts
keep it.

Triage measured one thing the report did not, and it decides the first question
this ticket asks. `is.na()` on the affected column:

| | local | dtplyr |
|---|---|---|
| input | `FALSE FALSE` | — |
| fixed `.by` key, result | `FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE` | `FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE` |
| passthrough column, result | `FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE` | `FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE` |

A value that was not missing becomes missing. That is a change to the column's
values and not only to its `levels` attribute, so ADR 0016's passed-through
clause — *attributes and classes of columns marginplyr does not rewrite* — does
not reach it: that clause is about class and attributes, and 0016 nowhere places
values on either side of its boundary because no verb was thought to change
them. Keeping an `NA` level apart from a missing value is the whole subject of
ADR 0012. **The answer to this ticket is code, and no ADR amendment.** Do not
amend ADR 0016; the maintainer decided this during triage, on the reasoning ADR
0023 gives against a second copy of an argument.

**Desired behavior:**

Each dtplyr line of the Reproduction prints what its local line prints — `[1]
"p" NA` and `[1] "a" NA` — with `is.na()` matching local in both cases. Nothing
else in the output changes, and no other backend's behavior changes: dtplyr is
the only kind granted `drops_na_factor_level_on_union`, duckdb drops such a
level on the way in and arrow refuses the column, both before any branch exists.

**Key interfaces:**

- `margin_column_info()` currently reads the selection proxy for the plan's
  dimensions alone and returns `factors` keyed to them. It must also return
  entries for the plan's fixed `.by` keys and for the input's other factor
  columns that cross the union. **This needs no new query.** For every kind that
  can restore factors, the selection proxy already holds all columns —
  `grouping_selection_proxy()` collects a zero-row copy of the whole input where
  `collect_selection_proxy` is granted, and returns the input itself otherwise —
  so the restriction to dimensions is a choice made when reading the proxy, not
  a query boundary. ADR 0002 is satisfied: this is a second read *of the one
  snapshot*, which is what that ADR asks for, not a second acquisition.
- `label_margin_branch()` and `restore_margin_factors()` both iterate the plan's
  dimensions. Both must iterate the widened set. A non-dimension column is the
  simpler case: it is present in every branch, so the omitted-dimension arm that
  writes a Margin label never applies to it, and its label is always missing, so
  it takes the `encodes_missing_label_factor()` route or no route at all.
- The `encode_missing_label` predicate itself is unchanged — an `NA` level, a
  union that drops one, and a backend that can encode missing values. It already
  narrows the widened set to the columns that need the round trip, so a wide
  input pays a `mutate()` only for columns actually at risk.
- `factor_info`'s meaning widens from *metadata for the Margin dimensions* to
  *metadata for the factor columns crossing the branch union*. Its header should
  say so; both sides of the route read one answer, and that property must
  survive the widening.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] The Reproduction in this issue prints four identical pairs of lines: `[1]
      "p" NA` for both `fixed .by key` lines and `[1] "a" NA` for both
      `passthrough` lines.
- [ ] `is.na()` on the `.by` key and on the passthrough column agrees between
      the local and dtplyr results for the Reproduction's data.
- [ ] Ordered-ness is preserved through the round trip for a non-dimension
      ordered factor carrying an `NA` level.
- [ ] A factor column with no `NA` level takes no new route: it is not encoded
      to character and not rebuilt, on any backend.
- [ ] `.margin_label_position` remains a no-op for these columns. No Margin
      label is added to a `.by` key or a passthrough column, on any position
      setting.
- [ ] Tests cover both the `.by` key and the passthrough case, requiring dtplyr
      alone — the one-backend policy in AGENTS.md's *Release matrix* — reached
      through `skip_if_suggest_absent()`, and paired with the local result the
      way the tests written for #408 pair theirs.
- [ ] `test-query-policy.R`'s snapshots are unchanged. No execution entry point
      is added; the proxy read this widens already happens.
- [ ] The existing #408 assertions still pass unmodified.

**Out of scope:**

- Any amendment to ADR 0016 or ADR 0012. Settled above.
- Any change to which backend kinds hold `drops_na_factor_level_on_union`, or
  to the duckdb and arrow behavior the capability comment describes as
  happening before a branch exists.
- Restoring any attribute other than factor levels and ordered-ness. ADR 0016
  forbids it, and `restore_margin_factors()` remaining the only place marginplyr
  rebuilds a column's type is what that ADR rests on.
- Widening the selection proxy read to a column type other than factor.

title: dtplyr backend drops a declared NA factor level from a column that is not a Margin dimension
